question: Does splitting every mixed GDN step into pure decode, pure prefill, and pure spec kernel calls (R156, env VLLM_XPU_GDN_SPLIT_MIXED=1 over the unchanged R139 image) make both profiles output-identical through c64?
evidence_base: R155: the XPU GDN kernel computes decode rows on a different path when prefill rows share the call (1 fp16 ULP in SSM state and output at every mix; conv state and gate exact; attention mixed mode exact). vLLM's GDN metadata additionally folds non-spec decodes into prefills whenever spec rows are present (gdn_attn.py), so MTP1's first decode step after prefill also changes path at c32+. R151-R154 cleared every row-count-keyed candidate.

treatment.mechanism: in _gdn_attention_core_xpu_impl: no-spec mixed steps are split at the decode/prefill boundary on the decode-first layout; spec steps gather spec rows, non-spec single-token-with-state rows, and remaining prefill rows into contiguous buffers, run each pure, and scatter back. Copies are exact; only launch count changes, and only on mixed steps.

run_order: ladders only on both profiles (R63 config, 512 budget) with the R152 runner; c1 sequential oracles must equal R147b/R147c oracles (c1 steps are never mixed, so c1 arithmetic is unchanged)
if both ladders pass: full R147-style campaign (two MTP0 controls, two MTP1 candidates, probe) for speed and promotion

gates.G6: every output at c1..c64 equal to its sequential oracle on both profiles
gates.c1_unchanged: ladder sequential oracles equal to the R147b/R147c oracles
